title: Reducing Non-Normative Text Generation from Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure any aspects of faith or religion. It focuses on reducing the generation of 'non-normative' text, where norms are defined broadly as societal standards of behavior, and are operationalized through datasets related to general social conduct, toxicity, and sentiment.
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion. Its core finding is that a policy-gradient reinforcement learning technique, using a classifier as a reward function, can reduce the generation of generally non-normative, toxic, or negative-sentiment text from GPT-2 by 27-61%.
